title: Bundle manifest
description: data/manifest.json: records how a bundle was made so that it can be audited, reproduced and merged: tool version, source folders, hashes of the input files, run settings, thresholds, the date and licence notes. Written by the export module. docs/data_contract.md section 6.

command.description: Command line that produced the bundle, with paths relative to the working directory.

libraries.description: Versions of numpy, scipy, gemmi, tmtools and the other libraries that shaped the numbers.

created.description: Date (and time) the bundle was written.

id.description: Stable id of this bundle: the sha256 of the sorted source hashes and the profile, first 16 hex characters. Review events refer to it.

pages.description: Page file names relative to the bundle root.

data.description: Data file names relative to the bundle root, by blob.

files.description: Every file of the bundle with its size and sha256.

reference_pdb.description: PDB id or name of the reference structure; empty when none was given.

reference_given.description: false when no full-length reference structure was given: the construct was the frame and the checks that need the rest of the protein did not run (caps_off says which).

sources.description: Every input file that went into the bundle, with its hash. Paths are file and folder names only: the exporter cuts every absolute path to its last component, so the folders of the machine that built the bundle are not recorded.

role.description: settings, csv, xlsx, accepted_structure, rejected_structure, target_structure, reference_structure, note, ...

run.description: Run id the file belongs to; absent for shared files.

count.description: For folders summarised in one entry: number of files.

reference.description: Public reference data used (UniProt entries, SIFTS, AlphaFold DB, ConSurf-DB) with url, retrieval date and hash, copied from data/reference/manifest.json. Only accessions and ids were ever sent to the network.

runs.description: Per run: reader, tool version, settings as read, the filter set, counts and the warnings the reader raised. The same settings and counts as campaign runs[], plus provenance.

settings_raw.description: The settings file as read, unchanged.

filter_set.description: Only for a run judged by the thresholds it recorded itself: source, n_rules, unevaluated (recorded thresholds on metrics Binderscope does not carry), unlimited (infinite thresholds: no limit) and a note.

counts.description: n_designs, n_accepted, n_rejected, n_families, funnel counts with their status.

annotations.description: What the reader worked out or found beside the run: the campaign modality (and the per-design counts behind it when they disagree), the scaffold it was built on, and what the xlsx files added - highlighted rows, sample names, notes.

caps.description: The capability flags of the profile as exported (copy of profile.caps), so tools can read what a bundle carries without opening the blobs.

caps_off.description: Why a context flag of caps (copy of profile.caps_off) is false, for the flags that compare a design with something outside the construct (olig, rest_ctx, glycan, membrane). Absent when none is off. A false flag in caps alone cannot say whether the check did not run or ran on nothing, and a reader deciding whether to trust a campaign needs to know which: no_reference means no full-length reference structure was given, so the check could not run and a design without a finding there was not tested; reference_lacks means a reference was given but holds nothing for the check, so it had nothing to test; profile means the profile switched the flag off. note is the specific reason in words.

thresholds.description: Thresholds that shaped numbers and verdicts: the check presets, the context thresholds, the diversity cut distances and the near-miss rule, as used (copy of profile.checks and diversity defaults).

interface.description: Distance cut-offs of the interface analysis: contact 4.5 A, hydrogen bond 3.5 A, salt bridge 4.0 A, ...

placement.description: How the designs were placed on the reference chain: mode (interface, whole or core, as chosen), fit (the target frame's name for it: interface, all or core), the weights of the interface fit (iface_full: CA this close to a binder atom weigh 1, in A; iface_decay: width of the Gaussian beyond it; iface_floor: the smallest weight; iface_cutoff: residues near the binder that deviate more than this are left out of the refit; iface_min_n: fewer residues near the binder than this and the whole-target fit is used), the weights from which a residue counts as near the binder (near_weight) and in the RMSD near the interface (report_weight), and warn_rmsd (A, the RMSD near the interface above which a warning is written).

validation.description: Result of the cross-checks run at build time: counts against the CSVs, recomputed against reported metrics (agreement), anything that did not match. Mismatches are listed, never hidden.

metric_agreement.description: metric -> {n, mean_abs_diff, max_abs_diff, r}: recomputed value in m against the tool's own column in src.

licences.description: Licence notes that travel with the bundle.

privacy.description: What left the machine while building: accessions, PDB ids, gene names and taxon ids only; never a binder sequence or a design id.
